cells.protocol_issues: Triangulation rule (two independent T1-T2 confirmations for load-bearing numbers) is unmeetable for composite index scores: WIPO is the sole originator; all secondary carriers (e.g., TheGlobalEconomy, T5) republish WIPO. cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior: prior recorded 23.7 (GII 2024, rank 86/133). Updated to GII 2025: score 24.7, rank 86/139 (edition released Sept 2025). cells.value: Operating agtech venture ecosystem: Egypt is one of Africa's 'big three' agrifoodtech markets (with Kenya and Nigeria); 22 agrifoodtech deals totalling USD 26M in 2024 (+2,775% YoY after a depressed 2023), vs USD 112M across 24 deals in 2022; named active cohort includes Mozare3, Zr3i, FreshSource, Cropsa, Baramoda, NileBot, Agrimatic Farms, Askova, Agristry, RoboCare, OneOrder, Cartona.
cells.source_title: AgFunder, Developing Markets AgriFoodTech Investment Report 2025 (Africa: investment by country p.49; top-funded companies pp.53-54; investor list p.80)
cells.quality_evidence: Top Egyptian rounds 2024: OneOrder USD 16M Series A (eGrocery; 3rd-largest round in Africa), Cartona USD 6M Series A, one Egyptian midstream-technologies company USD 8M across rounds, Seafood Factory USD 180K seed (AgFunder report pp.53-54). Active local investors/accelerators include Flat6Labs Egypt (5 deals, report p.80). Counterpoint (IFPRI policy note, Dec 2025, T2): developer landscape is 'fragmented, dominated by early-stage startups facing funding shortages', reliant on NGO/donor project cycles. UNDP Digital Agribusiness Map (2025) names regionally active startups across all four agro-ecological zones (Delta: Mozare3, Baramoda, NileBot, Agrimatic, FreshSource; Coastal: Dessaal, Hydrofarms, Yalla Mozare3, GoAgri; Upper Egypt: Shoura Seeds, MwaslaTech, IrriSat; Desert: DesertAgro, WASDEL, Palmatec, ReefTech).
cells.scale_evidence: 2024: USD 26M across 22 deals (AgFunder 2025 report p.49). 2022: USD 112M across 24 deals; H1 2023 collapse to ~USD 0.7M (AgFunder Africa data snapshot, Sept 2023, agfundernews.com/kenya-nigeria-and-egypt-lead-the-way-for-agrifoodtech-investment-in-africa). Kenya, Nigeria and Egypt cumulatively captured ~76% of African agrifoodtech funding over the past decade (AgFunder).
cells.search_trail: AgFunder Africa/Developing Markets reports (T4): located DM AgriFoodTech Investment Report 2025 PDF, extracted Egypt rows -> agfundernews data snapshots (Apr/May 2025; Sept 2023) for YoY context -> UNDP Digital Agribusiness Map Egypt 2025 (T2) for named cohort by region -> A2K4D/AUC 'AI Applications for Food Security in Egypt' (Mar 2025) Annex B startup table. Startup existence facts (Mozare3 pre-seed >USD 1M, 2021; FreshSource rounds) seen in T5 press (MENAbytes etc.) but values taken from T4 report only. Accessed 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Deep link for the AgFunder report resolves to a co-publisher mirror (omnivore.vc); AgFunder's own download page is email-gated. Press summaries cite 'Egypt: USD 317M across 159 deals over the decade' but this figure could not be located in the report PDF text — excluded as unverifiable.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior: prior cited an F6S directory count ('Dozens... 12+ notable'). Replaced with report-based deal/funding series. The 2,775% YoY jump reflects rebound from a collapsed 2023 base, not structural growth; funding remains far below the 2021-2022 peak.

cells.value: Multiple operating digital-agriculture partnerships with named partners: 'Agri Misr' e-platform (launched 13 Jul 2021: MALR + Ministry of Planning + Agricultural Bank of Egypt + eFinance Investment Group/eAswaaq); FAO x MALR El-Mufeed advisory app (2019-present); IFPRI x MALR (USAID-funded EIBC project) price-monitoring tool built into the private Mahsoly platform, launched 5 Jun 2024; Farmer Card/Meeza payment rails run by MALR with ABE and e-finance.
cells.source_title: IFPRI Policy Note (Dec 2025): Digital Agricultural Technology in Egypt — Insights from App Developers (Abdallah, Abdelhadi & Karachiwalla)
cells.tier: T2 (T5 for Agri Misr launch existence fact)
cells.quality_evidence: IFPRI x MALR collaboration under the USAID EIBC project produced and publicly launched the Mahsoly price-monitoring tool on 5 Jun 2024 (IFPRI/USAID/MALR note 'Digital Tools for Smallholders in Egypt', cgspace.cgiar.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/9186a484-d8a4-4da5-a6ee-659bea9456ee/content) — a concrete, operating public-research-private partnership. The AgriTech 2025 forum, convened by Egyptian ministries in 2025, issued a smart-agriculture roadmap explicitly stressing PPPs and digital extension modernisation (documented in the IFPRI Dec 2025 note, citing Egyptian Gazette 2025). FAO x MALR jointly promoted El-Mufeed to extension agents in all governorates (egypt.un.org/en/106025). Institutional caveat (IFPRI, T2): public-private coordination on agricultural DATA remains weak — public sector 'hesitant to share data with app developers'; PPPs exist for services but not yet for data infrastructure.
cells.scale_evidence: No consolidated reach figures published for any named PPP. Agri Misr user numbers not published. Farmer Card scale (4.2M cards; see 6.14) is government-run with banking partners rather than a PPP in the strict sense.
cells.search_trail: IFPRI Dec 2025 policy note (T2, read in full) -> IFPRI/USAID/MALR Mahsoly launch note (T2) -> FAO/UN Egypt pages for El-Mufeed partnership (T1) -> eFinance Investment Group corporate announcement for Agri Misr partners/launch date (T5, existence fact) -> searched sis.gov.eg for the Sept 2025 MALR-MCIT joint review cited by the prior desk pass: not located. Accessed 2026-08-22.

Agri Misr launch is only citable from corporate/press sources (T5-admissible existence fact); no T3 government page found for it.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior: prior anchored on the 2021 'Agri Egypt' launch and was flagged stale. Refreshed with 2024-2025 operating evidence (IFPRI x MALR tool launch Jun 2024; AgriTech 2025 ministerial roadmap; FAO x MALR ongoing). Also corrected platform name: corporate announcement calls it 'AGRI MISR' (Egyptian Digital Agricultural Network); press used 'Agri Egypt'.

cells.value: One registered digital public good is operating in Egyptian agriculture: El-Mufeed, the Egypt deployment of the FAO Digital Services Portfolio (a DPG listed on the Digital Public Goods Alliance registry), run with MALR since 2019 and promoted to extension agents in all governorates. No Egypt-developed agricultural DPG was found in the DPGA registry.
cells.source_title: FAO e-Agriculture: Proud Contributor Since 2022 — FAO in the 2025 State of the Digital Public Goods Ecosystem Report (DPGA registry includes the FAO Digital Services Portfolio)
cells.quality_evidence: Institutionalisation: FAO x MALR joint dissemination — virtual onboarding of extension agents from all governorates (148 participants: extension agents, researchers, academia, farmers, rural women, NGOs; egypt.un.org/en/106025). Developed participatorily with farmers and rural women; content expanded (30+ horticulture products, COVID-19 food-safety module) per FAO country-case page. FAO joined the DPGA in 2022 and promotes a DPG-first approach for agrifood digitalisation; its registry entries include the Digital Services Portfolio (of which El-Mufeed is the Egypt instance) and WaPOR (open water-productivity database covering Egypt).
cells.scale_evidence: Farm-management advisory platforms including 'the Digital Services Portfolio (El-Mufeed)' reach 'tens of thousands of users' (IFPRI policy note, Dec 2025, T2 — platform-reported figures). No El-Mufeed-specific audited user count published.
cells.search_trail: DPGA registry search for Egypt/agriculture DPGs (digitalpublicgoods.net/registry) -> FAO e-agriculture DPGA membership and 2025 ecosystem-report pages (T1) -> FAO Egypt El-Mufeed pages and FAO Digital Services Portfolio country-cases page confirming Egypt case (T1) -> UN Egypt news on FAO x MALR extension rollout (T1) -> IFPRI Dec 2025 note for reach (T2). Accessed 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Rung ambiguity: the DPG (FAO Digital Services Portfolio) is registered globally, and its Egypt instance (El-Mufeed) is operating nationally — but Egypt has not itself adopted a DPG policy or registered a national product. Recorded as Operating for the deployed-DPG reading; flag for definition clarification.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior: prior stated El-Mufeed and Hudhud are 'not formally registered DPGs'. Corrected: El-Mufeed is the Egypt deployment of the FAO Digital Services Portfolio, which IS a registered DPG on the DPGA registry; Hudhud remains government-proprietary (not a DPG).

cells.value: DATA GAP — no SME/agribusiness-specific digital-tool adoption percentage exists for Egypt. Searched in order: (1) CAPMAS/MCIT ICT-usage-in-enterprises survey (2019/20, economy-wide only: >70% of surveyed enterprises use computers/internet — no agribusiness breakout), as summarised in OECD 'SME and Entrepreneurship Policy in Egypt' (SME Digitalisation chapter); (2) World Bank Enterprise Surveys Egypt — no agricultural digital-tool adoption indicator; (3) UNDP Digital Agribusiness Map Egypt (2025) — publishes regional agri-tech adoption estimates (Delta 15%, Northern Coastal 10%, Upper Egypt 5%, Desert 3%) but these are farm-level regional estimates, not SME/agribusiness firm-level adoption; (4) IFPRI Dec 2025 policy note and A2K4D/AUC Mar 2025 report — qualitative only; (5) ITU DataHub — no enterprise agribusiness series.
cells.source_title: OECD, SME and Entrepreneurship Policy in Egypt — SME Digitalisation in Egypt chapter (closest checked source; no agribusiness-specific figure)
cells.search_trail: OECD SME digitalisation chapter (fetch returned 403; content confirmed via search excerpts citing the 2019/20 MCIT/CAPMAS enterprise survey) -> UNDP Digital Agribusiness Map 2025 PDF read in full (regional adoption panels) -> IFPRI Dec 2025 note -> A2K4D Mar 2025 report -> CAPMAS/ITU checks. Accessed 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Nearest-available data mismatch the indicator population two ways: MCIT/CAPMAS enterprise survey = all-sector SMEs (not agribusiness); UNDP regional agri-tech adoption (3-15%) = farm-level (not SME/agribusiness firms). Neither can be recorded as the indicator value without redefining it. OECD page blocked robotic fetch (403) — verified via search snippets only.
cells.notes: CONSISTENT with prior ('no SME-specific percentage located'), now with a documented trail. If the indicator definition were relaxed to farm-level regional agri-tech adoption, the UNDP 2025 range (3-15% by region) would put Egypt below the 10-25 band boundary in most regions.

cells.value: Operating agri-fintech rails with documented smallholder reach: national Farmer Card converted to a Meeza payment card on ABE/e-finance rails — 4.2 million smart farmer cards issued (Minister of Agriculture statement, 7 Nov 2024); ABE agricultural advances at preferential 5% accessible via the Meeza Farmer Card; private agri-fintech (Mozare3 with an NBE low-cost financing agreement; a farmer-facing platform documented by IFPRI offering interest-free harvest-linked finance to 5,000-6,000 active farmers/month).
cells.source_title: IFPRI Policy Note (Dec 2025): Digital Agricultural Technology in Egypt — Insights from App Developers (harvest-linked finance platform, 5,000-6,000 active farmers/month)
cells.tier: T2 (IFPRI facts); ministerial figures via T5 press carrier — flagged
cells.quality_evidence: System architecture: Farmer Card (since 2016) records landholding/quota/subsidy data and was converted to a Meeza payment instrument (CBE national payment scheme) with ABE and e-finance as rails. ABE offers agricultural advances at a preferential 5% rate through the Meeza Farmer Card linked to landholding certificates (ABE CEO statements, Nov 2025, via press). Enabling environment: CBE-led financial inclusion reached 71.5% of eligible adults by June 2024 (48.1M transactional accounts; CBE release of 15 Dec 2024 — cbe.org.eg fetch blocked by WAF, figure widely carried); mobile-money account ownership 15.6% of adults (Global Findex 2024, T1, recorded at indicator 8.4). Mozare3 signed an agreement with the National Bank of Egypt for low-cost farmer financing (Wamda/press, existence fact).
cells.scale_evidence: 4.2 million smart farmer cards issued; 20 digitised agricultural services on the Digital Egypt portal; 5,827 POS machines and 5,752 tablets deployed at agricultural cooperatives covering 8.2M feddans (Minister of Agriculture Alaa Farouk, 7 Nov 2024, as reported by Youm7 — official statement via T5 carrier, flagged). IFPRI-documented private platform: 5,000-6,000 active farmers/month receiving interest-free harvest-linked finance (T2, platform-reported).
cells.search_trail: IFPRI Dec 2025 note (T2) -> CBE financial-inclusion release (T1 target; WAF-blocked, noted) -> Findex 2024 via prior bundle -> ABE/Meeza: fintech-egypt.com (CBE-powered, 2019 — no farmer numbers) -> Arabic search for farmer-card counts -> Youm7 report of ministerial statement (4.2M cards, POS/tablet counts) -> Mozare3 scale: GSMA search (no case study found), AgFunder profile, Wamda/MENAbytes (existence only). Accessed 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: (1) The prior's '~6,300 smallholders financed by Mozare3' could not be verified in any T1-T4 source; a 2024-dated profile states 'over 35 contracted farms and more than 100 farmers' — figures conflict; Mozare3 scale left unrecorded. (2) The 4.2M farmer-card figure is a ministerial statement reachable only through press (T5 carrier of a T3 statement) — tier ambiguity; no MALR/SIS page located. (3) cbe.org.eg blocks robotic access; CBE figures could not be deep-verified at source.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior: Mozare3 reach figure dropped as unverifiable (see protocol_issues); scale evidence re-anchored on the government Farmer Card/Meeza system (4.2M cards) and the IFPRI-documented monthly-active financing platform. PREREQUISITE FIN: rails demonstrably present and operating with large-scale card issuance; the open question is active usage vs issuance.

cells.value: Multiple digital advisory platforms operating, several above 10k users (platform-reported, compiled by IFPRI): Mahsoly and AlMorshed Poultry 100K+ users each; several other advisory platforms 10K+; farm-management platforms Mazra3ty, Fila7a and El-Mufeed reach 'tens of thousands'; an IFPRI-interviewed marketplace app exceeds 100,000 users; a second farmer-facing app maintains 5,000-6,000 active farmers/month.
cells.source_title: IFPRI Policy Note (Dec 2025): Digital Agricultural Technology in Egypt — Insights from App Developers
cells.quality_evidence: Ecosystem breadth: 26 active and inactive apps compiled by IFPRI; active platforms span marketplaces, comprehensive farm-management advisors (Mazra3ty, Fila7a, El-Mufeed, Bashaier) and specialised crop/livestock advisors (Comprehensive Pomegranate/Olive Management, Chia, AlMorshed Poultry). Government-institutionalised channel: FAO x MALR El-Mufeed disseminated through extension agents in all governorates (T1). Sustainability caveats (T2): notable attrition — Early Climate Warning System, IRWI, Shary, Taswiq, Al-Nota and others now inactive; ICARDA diagnostic (cited in IFPRI note): of eight digital-tool categories only mobile apps and sensors are 'fairly widely used'; government apps (El-Mufeed, Hudhud, DAIRS) face uptake constraints.
cells.scale_evidence: Counts and who reports them: 100K+ (Mahsoly), 100K+ (AlMorshed Poultry), 10K+ (several advisory platforms), tens of thousands (Mazra3ty/Fila7a/El-Mufeed) — all platform-self-reported figures compiled in the IFPRI note; >100,000 users (IFPRI-interviewed 'App 1' marketplace) and 5,000-6,000 active farmers/month ('App 2') — developer-reported in IFPRI interviews. Utilisation caveat (IFPRI expert): 'only a small share of farmers actively use agricultural apps... consistent utilization is low' — registered-user counts likely overstate active use.
cells.search_trail: Prior lead 'ICARDA 2025 review' -> CGSpace search located IFPRI Dec 2025 policy note carrying the exact user-count claims (read in full, T2) -> FAO country-cases page for El-Mufeed (T1) -> IFPRI Egypt Agriculture Apps Repository (egyptssp.ifpri.info/agricultural-apps) noted as companion inventory. Accessed 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: All user counts are platform-self-reported; the T2 wrapper (IFPRI) compiles but does not independently verify them, and does not distinguish registered from active users. Prior desk pass attributed these figures to a 'CGIAR/ICARDA digital agriculture review 2025'; the locatable carrier is the IFPRI policy note (Dec 2025) — the ICARDA 2025 diagnostic it cites was not directly retrievable on CGSpace (only ICARDA 2023 'Current Situation of Digital Agriculture in Egypt').
cells.notes: CONFIRMS the prior's substance (Mahsoly and AlMorshed Poultry 100K+; several platforms 10K+) with the correct citation. The >10k 'at scale' bar is met by multiple platforms on reported counts, with the active-use caveat recorded.

cells.value: Multiple agricultural e-commerce/marketplace platforms operating: Mahsoly (crops and land marketplace with El-Obour wholesale price feed; >100K reported users), Mahaseel, Khodarcom, Khodar Supply, Cropsa (aggregation/market linkage), FreshSource (B2B fresh-produce supply chain), Tekeya, OneOrder (e-grocery/food service supply; USD 16M Series A in 2024), Cartona (B2B trade platform incl. food; USD 6M Series A in 2024).
cells.source_title: IFPRI Policy Note (Dec 2025): Digital Agricultural Technology in Egypt — Insights from App Developers
cells.quality_evidence: Mahsoly gained a formal price-monitoring tool developed by IFPRI with MALR under the USAID EIBC project, publicly launched 5 Jun 2024 (IFPRI/USAID/MALR note, T2) — evidence of institutional embedding. FreshSource and Mahsoly 'credited with reducing intermediaries and improving cold-chain efficiency, though empirical evaluations are limited' (IFPRI, T2). Investor validation 2024: OneOrder USD 16M Series A (3rd-largest African agrifoodtech round), Cartona USD 6M Series A (AgFunder DM report 2025, T4).
cells.scale_evidence: Mahsoly: >100K users (platform-reported, via IFPRI note; also matches the IFPRI-interviewed 'App 1' marketplace exceeding 100,000 users facilitating crop and land trading). No GMV or transaction-volume figures published for any platform in T1-T4 sources.
cells.search_trail: IFPRI Dec 2025 note (marketplace landscape; read in full) -> IFPRI/USAID/MALR Mahsoly price-tool launch note (T2) -> AgFunder DM AgriFoodTech report 2025 for 2024 rounds (T4). Prior lead 'Mozare3 ~6,300 financed' checked and moved to 6.14 issue log (unverifiable; also a financing metric, not e-commerce scale). Accessed 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: E-commerce scale beyond user counts (GMV, active buyers/sellers) is unpublished; user counts are platform-self-reported. Boundary question: OneOrder (restaurant supply e-grocery) and Cartona (general B2B FMCG) are food-value-chain rather than farmer-facing platforms — inclusion depends on indicator boundary; both flagged rather than silently counted.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior: prior mixed Mozare3's financing count into e-commerce evidence; removed. Presence and operation are well-documented; scale evidence rests on Mahsoly's reported 100K+ users plus 2024 investor validation.

cells.value: AI-enabled agricultural solutions deployed but with limited verified reach: Hudhud (MALR x MCIT Arabic AI assistant: chatbot + photo-based pest/disease identification), pilot-launched Dec 2021, live on Google Play (publisher MCIT), 'currently accessible to a select group of farmers participating in government-led digital transformation initiatives' (A2K4D, Mar 2025); MALR applies AI to weather forecasting, crop/soil-health monitoring and satellite plot-boundary identification in the Delta; private AI: Qamhawey (Mahaseel Masr) image-recognition agronomy app, Zr3i satellite-based crop analytics/insurance, Agristry crop mapping/drone analysis, RoboCare plant-disease detection.
cells.source_title: A2K4D/American University in Cairo (MENA AI Observatory), AI Applications for Food Security in Egypt: Practices, Opportunities, and Challenges (Nagla Rizk, March 2025)
cells.quality_evidence: Institutional frame: agriculture is a priority sector in the National AI Strategy (2nd edition 2025-2030, NCAI); MCIT Applied Innovation Center (est. 2020) works on applied AI. Hudhud is a formal MALR x MCIT collaboration (launch by both ministers, Dec 2021; Google Play publisher com.mcit.Hodhod). Private-sector AI documented across the A2K4D Annex B operator table (Mozare3, Zr3i, Askova, Agristry, RoboCare, Talpalabs, YieldX, Agrimatic, plus WFP Egypt using AI for food-security analytics). Corroboration (IFPRI Dec 2025, T2): Qamhawey described as AI-powered image recognition + real-time chat (per Entlaq 2024 industry report).
cells.scale_evidence: No verified user counts for any government AI deployment. Hudhud reach explicitly limited: 'accessible to a select group of farmers participating in government-led digital transformation initiatives, with plans for broader deployment pending further infrastructure development' (A2K4D, Mar 2025). ICARDA diagnostic (via IFPRI note): government-led apps incl. Hudhud face uptake constraints from digital literacy, data-security concerns and platform maintenance costs.
cells.search_trail: Hudhud launch: MCIT/MALR joint announcement (Dec 2021, via press; Google Play listing com.mcit.Hodhod confirms MCIT as publisher) -> A2K4D/AUC Mar 2025 report (downloaded, searched full text for Hudhud/AI deployments/consent) -> IFPRI Dec 2025 note (Qamhawey, ICARDA diagnostic) -> searched sis.gov.eg for the prior's 'MALR-MCIT AI satellite crop-mapping project reviewed Sept 2025': not located; nearest official evidence is EgSA satellites (MisrSat-2, Horus-1) supporting agricultural monitoring. Accessed 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Prior's anchor source ('SIS.gov.eg MALR/MCIT crop-mapping project review, Sept 2025') could not be located — the satellite/AI crop-mapping claim survives only in weaker form (A2K4D: satellite imagery for Delta plot boundaries and irrigation recommendations; EgSA satellite programmes). A2K4D is a university research-centre report — tiered T4 (not peer-reviewed), though commissioned under a governance research programme.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior: prior treated Hudhud + crop mapping as fully operating at level-4 strength. Verified picture is weaker: Hudhud operating but restricted to a pilot cohort (A2K4D, Mar 2025); the Sept 2025 crop-mapping review citation unverifiable. Multiple private AI solutions operating commercially.

cells.value: No agriculture/AI-specific consent or farmer-data-rights safeguards exist beyond the general regime. General regime now operational: PDPL 151/2020 became enforceable in practice with Executive Regulations issued by Minister of CIT Decree No. 816 of 2025 (1 Nov 2025; published 25 Dec 2025) and the Personal Data Protection Centre established; one-year compliance grace to ~Oct 2026. Egyptian Charter for Responsible AI (NCAI, Apr 2023, voluntary) contains zero agriculture/farmer references (full-text search) and a single consent clause ('express written consent from the data owner'). Draft AI law pending.
cells.source_title: Egyptian Charter for Responsible AI v1.0 (NCAI, 2023) — official PDF, ai.gov.eg (full-text searched: no agriculture/farmer provisions)
cells.quality_evidence: General safeguards (not ag-specific): (1) PDPL 151/2020 in force since 2020; Executive Regulations (Decree 816/2025) issued 1 Nov 2025, in force 2 Nov 2025, transforming the PDPL 'from a principles-based framework into a functioning supervisory regime'; Personal Data Protection Centre (PDPC) operationalised as independent authority under MCIT; licensing portal expected ~mid-June 2026; full enforcement ~Oct 2026 (CMS legal update; Kluwer Global Privacy Law Review 2026 article GPLR2026009, T2). (2) Egyptian Charter for Responsible AI (Apr 2023, voluntary; launched by NCAI/MCIT). (3) National AI Strategy 2nd edition (2025-2030) embeds responsible-AI principles; draft AI law under development to convert voluntary principles into binding requirements (OECD.AI / Regulations.AI records). Relevant sector fact (IFPRI Dec 2025, T2): farmer distrust over 'data usage' and public-sector reluctance to share agricultural data are documented adoption barriers — no instrument addresses farmer data rights specifically.
cells.scale_evidence: Not applicable at Absent rung for the ag-specific instrument. PDPC enforcement track record: none yet (grace period runs to ~Oct 2026).
cells.search_trail: Egyptian Charter for Responsible AI PDF downloaded from ai.gov.eg and full-text searched for 'agricultur/farmer/consent' (0/0/1 hits) -> PDPL executive-regulations status: search located Decree 816/2025 coverage (CMS, Baker McKenzie, Chambers, Kluwer GPLR 2026) -> OECD AI Review of Egypt (2024) and UNESCO observatory pages checked for ag-specific AI governance: none -> A2K4D Mar 2025 report searched for farmer data rights/consent: none. Accessed 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Rung ambiguity flagged: the indicator demands ag/AI-specific provisions 'beyond the general DP law' — recorded Absent on that strict reading, while the general regime materially strengthened (exec regs + PDPC, Nov 2025). If the instrument intends general-safeguards-applicable-to-ag, the rung would be Adopted/Operating-pending-enforcement. Decree 816/2025 gazette text not directly linkable; cited via law-firm analyses (T4) and a peer-reviewed privacy-law article (T2).
cells.notes: MAJOR DIVERGENCE from prior: prior recorded PDPL as a 2020 paper framework (stale, no executive regulations). As of Nov 2025 the executive regulations are issued and the PDPC exists — the general data-protection prerequisite is now operational (with enforcement starting ~Oct 2026). The ag/AI-specific safeguard remains absent; the Responsible-AI Charter's silence on agriculture is now verified against the official text rather than assumed.

bundle_issues: (1) Index-owner statistics defeat the two-independent-T1/T2 triangulation rule: WIPO GII scores (6.1) have no independent second source by construction — all republishers derive from WIPO. Suggest a protocol carve-out for statistics whose originator is the sole authority. (2) Platform user counts across 3.9/3.10/6.12 are platform-self-reported and enter the record through T2 compilations (IFPRI Dec 2025) that do not independently audit them; registered-vs-active distinction is never made. Recommend a standing 'reported-by' convention for reach figures.
